notes: Intel publishes no 50-state breakdown. Its April 2025 U.S. fact sheet (company-hosted PDF) gives investment figures for its four manufacturing states only (Oregon, Arizona, New Mexico, Ohio); no newer edition found (checked 2026-11-24). The live intel.com usa-chipmaking page (moved from /usa-chipmaking/home.html, which now redirects) is undated and shows slightly higher cumulative figures ($65B Oregon since 1974, $34.5B Arizona since 1979, $17.68B New Mexico since 1980) plus 2023 state GDP contributions; the dated fact sheet is kept, and the page is cited only for the site descriptions. Cumulative investment and new-project figures are different measures and must not be added. The fact sheet also lists CHIPS Act awards per state (AZ $3.94B, NM $500M, OR $1.86B, OH $1.5B); these are government funding to Intel, not Intel's footprint, and are not recorded. Nationally, the usa-chipmaking page says Intel directly employs 45k people in the U.S. (company-published); not recorded as a row because the U.S. row's source is the 10-K PP&E table. A 2021 third-party study (FY2019 data) covering AZ, CA, NM and OR exists but is far older and was not used. PP&E by country is from the FY2025 10-K (Dec 27, 2025). 10-K Properties gives only square feet: U.S. 37 million (35 owned, 2 leased) vs other countries 28 million; there are no per-state or per-country site counts, so the 10-K's key production fabs (Oregon, Arizona, Ireland, Israel) and key assembly and test sites (China, New Mexico, Vietnam, Malaysia) appear as sites. The Costa Rica assembly and test site was removed: the FY2025 10-K no longer lists it and says Intel initiated the consolidation of its Costa Rican assembly and test operations into larger existing sites in Vietnam and Malaysia. The same passage says Intel slowed construction of the Ohio fab and discontinued planned expansions in Germany and Poland.
